record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.original_question: Describe which types of equations or systems of equations over a finite semigroup admit an algorithm that, for arbitrary values of the constants, decides whether the system is solvable in some finite extension of the original semigroup.

evidence.quote:
Problem 1.1. (S. Kublanovsky, M. Sapir) Describe the types of equations or systems of equations
for which there exists an algorithm that decides for any values of the constants whether the given
system is solvable in some finite extension of the original semigroup.

             Potential properties of semigroups include embedding problems into various recursive
classes of finite semigroups. A homomorphic image of a subsemigroup T of a semigroup S is called
a divisor of S (or factor of S).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a finite semigroup, and let $\mathcal{E}$ be a class of equations (or systems of equations) of a specified syntactic type with constants drawn from $S$ and unknowns ranging over an extension of $S$. Say that a system $\Sigma \in \mathcal{E}$ is potentially solvable over $S$ if there exists a finite semigroup $T$ containing $S$ as a subsemigroup such that $\Sigma$ has a solution in $T$. 

Characterize the syntactic types $\mathcal{E}$ of equations or systems of equations for which there exists an algorithm with the following property: given any finite semigroup $S$ and any system $\Sigma \in \mathcal{E}$ whose constants take arbitrary values in $S$, the algorithm decides whether $\Sigma$ is potentially solvable over $S$ (i.e., solvable in some finite semigroup extending $S$).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent compilation of unsolved problems in semigroup theory (Lyapin's notebook). It is closely related to Rhodes's 1966 problem on potential divisibility, which Kublanovsky and Sapir showed to be undecidable; however, the general classification problem of which types of equations admit a decidability algorithm remains open.

status_evidence.title: Minsky Machines and Algorithmic Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Kublanovsky and Sapir gave a negative answer to Rhodes's question on potential divisibility in finite semigroups.
status_evidence.claim: Related potential divisibility question is shown undecidable, but the general classification of decidable types remains open.
